c.tagline: Golden light, late nights, and endless plazas

hood_landmark.Malasaña: Plaza del Dos de Mayo, heart of the barrio's indie and vintage scene
hood_landmark.Chueca: Plaza de Chueca, hub of Madrid's LGBTQ+ nightlife
hood_landmark.La Latina: El Rastro Sunday flea market and the Cava Baja tapas street
hood_landmark.Salamanca: Calle de Serrano's 'Golden Mile' of luxury shopping
hood_landmark.Lavapiés: La Tabacalera cultural center amid multicultural street art

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing around Sol, Gran Vía, El Retiro and on the metro.
Livelier and rougher after dark — usual big-city caution.

hood_desc: Bohemian and hip, Malasaña is the heart of Madrid nightlife with indie bars, vintage shops and street art, ideal for young travelers and night owls.
Chueca is Madrid's vibrant, stylish LGBTQ+ quarter, packed with trendy restaurants, cocktail bars and boutiques, great for nightlife and a lively social scene.
La Latina is the old medieval quarter famous for tapas crawls and the Sunday El Rastro flea market, perfect for foodies and those wanting classic Madrid atmosphere.
Salamanca is the upscale, elegant district of designer boutiques, fine dining and grand architecture, suited to luxury shoppers and travelers wanting a refined base.
Lavapiés is Madrid's most multicultural, edgy neighborhood with cheap ethnic eats, galleries and a gritty creative vibe, appealing to budget and adventurous visitors.

water.note: Tap water is safe and among the best-rated in Europe.

transit.pay: Since June 2026 you can tap a contactless bank card or phone straight at Metro turnstiles, and EMT buses take contactless too. Alternatively buy a rechargeable Multi Card (2.50 EUR, ~US$3) from any metro station machine, the airport or tobacconists and load singles (1.50-2 EUR) or a 10-trip ticket. Airport metro trips carry a 3 EUR supplement.
transit.hours: Metro runs 6am-1:30am every day; after that, night owl buses fan out from Plaza de Cibeles.

landmarks: Puerta del Sol
Madrid's bustling central plaza, home to the famous Tio Pepe sign and the clock that rings in the Spanish New Year, marking kilometer zero of Spain.
Plaza Mayor
A grand 17th-century arcaded square with symmetrical facades and frescoed buildings, long the ceremonial and social heart of the city.
Royal Palace of Madrid
Western Europe's largest royal palace by floor area, showcasing opulent state rooms and a vast collection of art and armor.
Museo del Prado
One of the world's finest art museums, housing masterworks by Velazquez, Goya, and Bosch in a stately neoclassical building.
Gran Via
Madrid's grand, theater-lined boulevard nicknamed the 'Spanish Broadway,' celebrated for its early-20th-century architecture and bright lights.
Buen Retiro Park (Crystal Palace)
A vast historic park centered on a glass-and-iron Crystal Palace beside a lake, offering one of Madrid's most photogenic scenes.
Fountain of Cibeles
An iconic neoclassical fountain depicting the goddess Cybele in a lion-drawn chariot, serving as a favored spot for celebrating major victories.
Almudena Cathedral
Madrid's cathedral beside the Royal Palace, notable for its eclectic mix of Gothic, Baroque, and modern design and colorful ceiling.
Temple of Debod
An authentic ancient Egyptian temple gifted to Spain, dramatically relocated to a Madrid park and famed for its sunset reflections in the pool.
Santiago Bernabeu Stadium
The iconic home stadium of Real Madrid, a landmark for football fans and a striking piece of modern sports architecture.

train.note: No direct cross-border trains run from Madrid. For France you change at Barcelona onto the Renfe AVE services to Lyon and Marseille (or the SNCF TGV to Paris); the once-daily direct Madrid-Lisbon 'Lusitania' sleeper remains withdrawn, so Portugal now means a change (Renfe Alvia to the border) or a direct coach. Renfe runs domestic AVE high-speed trains nationwide, with private operators Iryo and Ouigo also on the busiest lines.

bus.note: International and long-distance coaches mostly use Estacion Sur (Mendez Alvaro). Alsa runs the direct Madrid-Lisbon/Porto services and routes into France and Morocco; FlixBus covers a wide European network.

ferry.note: Madrid is landlocked, so there are no ferries. For boats to the Balearics, Canaries or Morocco you first travel to a coastal port such as Valencia, Barcelona or Algeciras.
